arguments.root_cause_statement: The Deployment fraud/fraud-scoring asks for 512 whole CPU cores per pod. Its pod template sets .spec.template.spec.containers[scorer].resources.requests.cpu to "512" (512 cores) where the intended value is almost certainly "512m" (half a core). The only node in the cluster, incident-lab-control-plane, has 6 allocatable CPUs, so the scheduler cannot place the pod on any node and the pod fraud-scoring-596445859d-thcdh stays Pending with PodScheduled=False and a FailedScheduling event reading "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu". Because no pod is ever admitted, the Deployment reports ready=0/1 and no fraud scores are produced. There is no ResourceQuota or LimitRange in the namespace and the node is Ready and untainted, so nothing other than the oversized CPU request blocks scheduling.
arguments.mechanism: The Deployment fraud/fraud-scoring sets .spec.template.spec.containers[scorer].resources.requests.cpu to "512" — 512 whole cores instead of the intended "512m" — which exceeds the 6 allocatable CPUs of the cluster's only node, so its pod is rejected by the scheduler with FailedScheduling "Insufficient cpu" and stays Pending with PodScheduled=False, leaving the Deployment at ready=0/1.

evidence.claim: The Deployment has no ready replicas and its only pod is unscheduled.
The pod is Pending and has never been assigned a node.
The scheduler rejects the pod for lack of CPU on the single node.
The Deployment pod template carries the oversized CPU request that a human must edit.
The only node in the cluster has 6 CPUs allocatable, far below the 512-core request.

ruled_out.alternative: A ResourceQuota or LimitRange in the fraud namespace blocking or mutating the pod
ruled_out.ruling_claim: No ResourceQuota and no LimitRange objects exist in the namespace, so admission policy is not involved.
ruled_out.quote: 0 objects of kind limitranges in namespace fraud

ruled_out.alternative: The node is NotReady or tainted so nothing can schedule there
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The single node reports Ready=True with no taints listed, so node health is not the blocker.

ruled_out.alternative: An image pull failure or crashing container inside the pod
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod was never scheduled to a node, so no container was ever started; the only condition is PodScheduled=False.
